title: Welfare and health: changes-only pilot, arm A (current wording)
question: Which record shows stronger support for government-guaranteed health coverage and income support for the general population?
weighing: Judge the changes a record supports or opposes, whether it enacted them in government, voted on them, pressed for them, or seeks them, by their direction and size. Judge the size of what a record supports, not what it had the power to achieve: a record that backs every change in one direction put before it and seeks larger ones supports more change in that direction than one that enacted smaller changes. The tier shows how firmly an item commits the actor, not how large the change is; where a record's items point in opposite directions, the higher tier governs. A vote against a change counts as support for what the change would have removed, unless the record shows it opposed the change for not going far enough, for example by backing more generous versions of it; then it counts as support for going further. The health coverage and income support a record inherited are not part of its position.
highPole: government guarantees broad health coverage and income support
lowPole: government's role in health coverage and income support is cut back

Changes to income support in the period

items.text: Voted against a budget that reduced public health spending by about 5 percent.
Publicly pressed fellow legislators to drop a proposed charge for doctor visits.
Voted for a law that raised the minimum public pension by about 10 percent.
Announced the intention to introduce a bill adding dental and eye care to public coverage.
Voted for extending subsidies for private insurance premiums for middle-income households.
Voted against a bill extending public health coverage to all residents.
Voted against a bill narrowing eligibility for existing public health coverage.
Voted for stricter job-search conditions on unemployment benefits, with benefit levels unchanged.
Voted for a budget that reduced funding for public health coverage by about 30 percent and ended that coverage for low-income adults without children.
Voted against extending subsidies for health insurance premiums.
Voted to reduce food and unemployment assistance by about 30 percent and to limit both to two years.
Voted to raise the pension age by three years.
Introduced a bill to replace public health coverage for older residents with a fixed payment toward private insurance.
Publicly urged fellow legislators to turn the remaining public health funding into fixed grants that grow more slowly than costs.
